#### Shiki’s Realism (*Shasei*)
Masaoka Shiki revolutionized haiku by promoting *shasei* (sketching from life). This haiku is a prime example. Rather than using grand metaphors, he focuses on a minute, objective detail: one leaf. Writing during the Meiji era, Shiki was often bedridden with tuberculosis. His observations of small changes in his garden—like a single leaf falling—were often mirrors of his own fragile health and his acute awareness of the passage of time.
